draft.title: Range and time of flight
card: Range is the horizontal distance a projectile travels. Time of flight is how long it stays in the air. Both depend on launch speed and launch angle.
Split the launch velocity into parts. Horizontal: vx = v cos θ. Vertical: vy = v sin θ. The vertical part decides the time of flight, and the horizontal part is constant.
For a launch from level ground with no air resistance, time of flight = 2v sin θ ÷ g. Range = vx × time of flight = v² sin 2θ ÷ g.
A larger launch speed gives a greater range and a longer time. For a fixed speed, 45° gives the longest range. A steeper angle gives a longer time in the air.
draft.remember: Vertical motion sets the time in the air. Range is horizontal speed times that time, and 45° gives the longest range.

a.q: Two balls are kicked from level ground at the same speed, one at 30° and one at 60°. Ignoring air resistance, which statement is correct?
opts: The 60° ball is in the air longer
The 30° ball is in the air longer
Both balls are in the air for the same time
The 60° ball travels much further than the 30° ball
a.why: The 60° ball has the larger vertical velocity, v sin θ, so it stays up longer. The ranges are equal, because sin 60° and sin 30° give the same value of sin 2θ. The 60° ball is not the one that goes further.
a.clue: Which angle gives the larger vertical part of the velocity?

b.q: Priya kicks a ball from level ground at 20 m/s. She wants the greatest range and ignores air resistance. Which launch angle should she choose?
opts: 45°, which makes sin 2θ largest
30°, so the ball keeps more horizontal speed
60°, so the ball stays in the air longer
90°, so the ball reaches the greatest height
b.why: Range is v² sin 2θ ÷ g, and sin 2θ is largest at 45°. A steeper angle gives more time in the air but less horizontal speed, and a flatter angle does the reverse. A 90° launch goes straight up and has no range.
b.clue: Range depends on both horizontal speed and time in the air.

a.best: The 60° ball is in the air longer

problems.detail: The why says "sin 60° and sin 30° give the same value of sin 2θ", which is garbled. The equal ranges come from sin 2θ being sin 120° and sin 60°, which are equal. As written, it could confuse students about what is being substituted into sin 2θ.
